articles.title: PostgreSQL Explained: The Database You Default To
articles.excerpt: Introduction Ask experienced developers which database to pick for a new project, and one answer comes up more than any other: PostgreSQL, usually called Postgres. It is free, open source, battle-test…
articles.body: Introduction Ask experienced developers which database to pick for a new project, and one answer comes up more than any other: PostgreSQL, usually called Postgres. It is free, open source, battle-tested for decades, and now the most loved database in developer surveys. If the SQL joins post taught you how to ask questions of data, this one explains where that data should live. Tables, rows, and relationships Postgres is a relational database: data lives in tables of rows and columns, and tables relate to each other by keys.
articles.author: The Practical Developer

articles.title: Prompt Injection Defense for Production Agents: What Actually Works
articles.excerpt: Prompt injection cannot be reliably filtered, and any defense built on detecting malicious text will eventually lose. What works in production is architectural: separate instructions from data, strip…
articles.body: Prompt injection cannot be reliably filtered, and any defense built on detecting malicious text will eventually lose. What works in production is architectural: separate instructions from data, strip privileges until an injected instruction has nothing to act on, gate irreversible actions behind humans, and design the blast radius before the attack instead of after it. This article is the defense stack we deploy with every client system, and why each layer exists. § 01 · The problem, stated honestly A language model has one input channel. Instructions and data travel down the same pipe, and the model has no hardware-level way to tell them apart.
articles.author: orbiresearch

articles.title: Read the migration before production does: miglens, a local-AI migration-risk explainer in Go
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine miglens reads a SQL migration and tells you what is risky about it before you run it: first with a dete…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built miglens reads a SQL migration and tells you what is risky about it before you run it: first with a deterministic rule scan, then in plain English from a local open-weight model. miglens migrations/0042_orders_cleanup.sql cat migration.sql | miglens -model llama3.2:1b The dangerous line in a migration is rarely a syntax error. It is the DROP COLUMN that deletes data a still-running service needs, the ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL that fails on a table with two million rows, the CREATE INDEX that quietly blocks writes for twenty minutes. Linters check style. miglens checks blast radius.
articles.author: Parsa Aftabi

articles.title: Chitthi: A Séance Where the Ghost Can Only Quote Itself
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Chitthi (चिट्ठी, Hindi for "a letter") lets you ask questions of people who left letters behind and hea…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Chitthi (चिट्ठी, Hindi for "a letter") lets you ask questions of people who left letters behind and hear the answer in their own words. Literally their own words: the ghost may only quote what it actually wrote. Most "talk to a historical figure" chatbots are confident ventriloquists. Ask one about Nehru and you get a fluent paragraph with a quote that sounds right and appears nowhere. For a séance, that is the wrong kind of spooky. Chitthi works the other way round. It reads scanned letters page by page, indexes them on your own machine, and answers only from the passages it retrieves: Archivist mode answers in the third person and cites every claim.
articles.author: Om Kumar

articles.title: Rainy Season and a Phone Security Camera: Why It Says 'Moisture Detected' and Stops Charging, Why the Lens Fogs, and How to Keep It Recording Offline
articles.excerpt: Short answer: In humid or rainy weather, an old phone used as a security camera usually fails at the charging port first, not at the camera. Samsung's support page says its phones "will not charge if…
articles.body: Short answer: In humid or rainy weather, an old phone used as a security camera usually fails at the charging port first, not at the camera. Samsung's support page says its phones "will not charge if moisture is present in the charging port," and that the water "will naturally evaporate from the charging port within approximately 1 to 2 hours." Google's Pixel help page describes the same protection with a different message: "Liquid or debris in USB port." For those hours the phone runs on its battery while the cable is still plugged in. If the battery is old, the camera can go dark before the port dries. The fix is mostly about where you put the phone and how the cable reaches it, not about buying anything.

articles.body: Possessing fortune-mod: Bringing an abandoned UNIX oracle back from the dead For Hacktober Week 4's "Ghost in the Machine" challenge, I decided to bring something forgotten back to life. Not a person, but a program. The Story In the quiet corners of UNIX history, fortune-mod sat forgotten. A simple oracle that once amused generations of hackers with its dry wit and groan-worthy puns, it had been left behind as computing moved on. For Día de los Muertos and Halloween, we remember not just the people who came before us, but the programs too. Like candles on an ofrenda, these forgotten tools deserve to be brought back to life.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Noctilucent Clouds over Sweden Explanation: Sometimes it’s night on the ground but day in the air. As the Earth rotates to eclipse the Sun, sunset rises up from the ground. Therefore, at sunset on the ground, sunlight still shines on clouds above. Under usual circumstances , a pretty sunset might be visible, but unusual noctilucent clouds float so high up they can be seen well after dark.

articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.
